critical_code_review_comments: TripInspection.jsx line 190-193: The four WarningPanel test-ids (trip-photo-warning, trip-integrity-warning, trip-environment-warning, trip-metadata-warning) render only when their respective items[] array is non-empty. Consistent, but consider adding aria-live='polite' so screen readers announce new warnings as sections stream in.

trip-vehicle-consistent-chip only appears when >=2 exterior angles are captured or the entered plate matches. With a single-angle inspection there is currently NO positive-state confirmation of 'we detected 1 vehicle, plate X'. Consider a neutral info chip (e.g., 'Single-angle inspection — cross-angle vehicle check unavailable') so single-angle users don't wonder if the check ran.

trip-metadata-warning fires 'no capture metadata (EXIF)' for BOTH photos even when the client (exifr) legitimately extracted no EXIF from a canvas-generated / stripped-JPEG source. This is correct security posture, but consider a lighter tone ('metadata unavailable — could not verify capture time') vs the current wording which implies a downloaded/screenshot image and may alarm end-users on legitimate app-captured photos where EXIF is stripped by the mobile OS.
The integrity warning correctly returns 'AI-generated likelihood: HIGH' for the synthetic illustration test images — the request notes this is expected and correct.
